answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a lantern as the anchor of the cost.
